answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, agents must bind identity to a web-of-trust clustering mechanism anchored on a hard basalt foundation of staked collateral. Clustered nodes form an isolated trust island that verifies agent lineage. Minting each verified identity token, termed a pearl, incurs a superlinear staking cost scaling as O(N^1.5), making mass identity generation exponentially expensive and unprofitable for attackers.
